title: Implemented matrix detectors are not default-approved public rules
symptom: The development aligner handles the requested return columns and the exact two-row Array.from/rows.filter example, but public format refuses both positive scenarios with FORMAT_NOT_ELIGIBLE and no matching convention. Their exact lookup keys are absent from the two-rule recommended preset. The later Python calculation envelope is also detected by the installed local and Windows candidate but remains unknown; Guide is empty and Align refuses without modifying bytes.

rootCause.summary: Detector support and public write authorization are separate. Existing TS/Python approvals do not cover the new return-guard and member-call-envelope keys; source-test success cannot authorize these keys. The new Python assignment-value axis likewise cannot inherit the simple-assignment approval.

requestedOutcome: After explicit bounded rule and example-license decisions, ship matching proof records and verify installed public Align preview/apply/recheck on the exact requested scenarios and counterexamples. Until then report the approval gap explicitly.
decisions: Preserve the two existing approvals unchanged; do not infer a new rule or license from implementation success.

Use the exact two-row member-call example from the user. It uses the same envelope key as differing-arity calls; the initial proposed three-row minimum was corrected to the measured two-row policy before seeking approval.
